mainTopic: Whether a son who robbed his father can forgive the theft debt to himself once he inherits, and three ways to explain the sources
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה, which finishes the case of a father who vowed that his son may not benefit from his property, even after the father's death. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה's case of a son who robbed his father. רב יוסף says the son may even give the payment to charity, and רב פפא adds that he must say 'This is what was stolen from my father.' The גמרא asks why the son, who is now the heir, cannot just forgive the debt to himself, since another משנה shows that a theft debt can be forgiven. רבי יוחנן answers that the two משניות follow two תנאים, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא. He bases this on a ברייתא about a man who robbed a גר, which ends in a disagreement between them. רב ששת objects to this reading and says instead that both משניות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי: forgiving works 'to others' but not 'to himself'. רבא gives the reverse answer and says both משניות follow רבי עקיבא, using the same split.

steps.title: A son forbidden from his father's property in life and in death
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its case: if a father vowed that his son may not benefit from his property, both in life and after death, the son may not inherit him. He passes his share on to his own sons or brothers. If he has nothing to live on, he borrows, and the lenders collect from his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father's vow covered both his life and his death, then when the father dies the son does not inherit him. He gives his share to his own sons or brothers. If he has no money of his own, he borrows, and the lenders come and collect their payment from that share.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the משנה. It shows what happens when a son is forbidden by a vow to benefit from his father's property, even after the father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow that covers 'in his death' stays in force after the father dies, so the son cannot take the inheritance himself. The share goes to the son's own heirs or brothers instead. If he is poor, he may borrow, and the lenders are paid from that share, which helps him only indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: In his life and in his death. The vow covers both periods.
Creditors, the people he owes money to

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about the robbery case. It finishes a separate case in the משנה about a father's vow. The גמרא goes back to the robbery case in the next step.

phrases.english: [If the father vowed his son may not benefit from his property] in his life and in his death,
if he dies, he does not inherit him,
and he gives it back to his sons or to his brothers.
phrases.notes: 'His' here means the son's own children or brothers.

phrases.english: And if he does not have [enough to live on],
he borrows, and the creditors come and collect payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּחַיָּיו וּבְמוֹתוֹ, אִם מֵת – לֹא יִירָשֶׁנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the vow covers life and death, the son may not inherit. His share goes to his sons or brothers. If he is poor, he borrows and the lenders collect from that share.

steps.title: The payment may even go to charity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. רב יוסף says the son who robbed his father may even put the payment into a charity fund.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יוסף said: He may even put it into a charity purse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a son who robbed his father. רב יוסף rules that, besides paying the other heirs, the son may give the money to charity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the son pays the stolen amount and the extra fifth to his sons or brothers. רב יוסף widens this: giving the money to charity also works. The main point is that the son must not keep it for himself.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Yosef said:
Even into a charity purse.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the משנה's earlier case: the son who robbed his father and has to pay it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲפִילּוּ לְאַרְנָקִי שֶׁל צְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא and goes back to the robbery case from earlier in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son may give the payment for his father's theft to charity.

steps.title: He must say the money is what he stole from his father
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that when the son gives the money, he must say 'This is what I stole from my father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And he must say: 'This is what was stolen from my father.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a condition to רב יוסף's ruling. The son has to state clearly that this money is repayment for robbing his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply handing over the money is not enough. By saying it out loud, the son shows the money is a return of stolen property and not an ordinary gift. That makes it count as paying back the theft.

keyTerms.meaning: What was stolen from my father

steps.whatToRemember: A son who robbed his father may pay it back to the other heirs or to charity, but he must say: 'This is what I stole from my father.'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And he must say:
'This is what was stolen from my father.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a requirement to רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When paying, the son must say the money is what he stole from his father.

steps.title: Why can't the heir just forgive the debt to himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the son is now the heir, so the debt is owed to him. Why can't he just forgive it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let him forgive it to himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the son has to pay anyone at all. As the heir, he is the person the debt is now owed to, so he should be able to cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the person who is owed money can forgive the debt. Once the father dies, the son stands in the father's place. So the משנה's demand that he pay others looks hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him forgive it to himself

phrases.english: Why?
Let him forgive it to himself!
phrases.notes: Since he is the heir, the debt is now owed to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's basic ruling that the son must pay others.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a son who robbed his father must pay it to his sons, brothers or charity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heir is the one the debt is owed to, and whoever is owed money can forgive it.

steps.title: Another משנה shows a theft debt can be forgiven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a משנה that talks about an owner forgiving the robber the principal but not the extra fifth. So a theft debt can clearly be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn: 'If he forgave him the principal but did not forgive him the fifth'? Clearly it can be forgiven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for its question. It quotes a משנה showing that an owner can forgive a robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה describes an owner forgiving the principal of a theft. So a theft debt is the kind of thing that can be forgiven. If so, the heir should be able to forgive it to himself, which makes the challenge stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, the value of what was stolen
The added fifth paid by a robber who swore falsely

phrases.english: Didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]:
If he forgave him the principal
phrases.notes: This משנה, on 103a, is about a robber who swore falsely and later admitted it.

phrases.english: but did not forgive him the fifth?
Clearly it can be forgiven!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא תְּנַן: מָחַל לוֹ עַל הַקֶּרֶן וְלֹא מָחַל לוֹ עַל הַחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 4 with an earlier משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the son should be able to forgive the theft debt to himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 103a: 'If he forgave him the principal but did not forgive him the fifth'

steps.title: The two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that there is no contradiction. One משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is not a problem. This one follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, and that one follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. He explains that the two משניות come from two תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that allows forgiveness follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that such a debt can be forgiven. Our משנה, which makes the son pay others, follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that it cannot. So the contradiction is solved by assigning each משנה to a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... that one (pairing each source with an opinion)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, whether a son can forgive his father's theft debt to himself depends on a dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי (it can be forgiven) and רבי עקיבא (it cannot), and our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. רב ששת and רבא later explain it differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is not a problem;
this one follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the משנה that allows forgiveness.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is our משנה, where the son cannot forgive it to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 4 and 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the two sources to two disputing תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות follow one opinion, so a theft debt can always be forgiven, and the heir could forgive it to himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה that allows forgiveness follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who holds that the son cannot forgive it to himself.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: the פסוק is about robbing a convert
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא. It first explains that the פסוק about a victim with 'no relative' must be talking about a גר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'If the man has no relative to whom the guilt payment can be returned.' Is there any Jew who has no relatives? So the פסוק must be talking about robbing a גר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יוחנן's answer. This opening part only sets the stage: it shows that the case is about robbing a גר who has no heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every Jew comes from יעקב, so every Jew has some relative who would inherit him. The only person with truly no heirs is a גר who has no Jewish children. This sets up the case where the מחלוקת will come out.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative who would receive a payment or inherit
Here, the payment owed for the theft

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
"But if the man has no kinsman
to whom the guilt payment can be returned"
But is there any person in Israel
who has no kinsmen?
Rather, about robbing a convert
the verse is speaking

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that holds the מחלוקת רבי יוחנן pointed to in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the two משניות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading במדבר 5:8 as talking about robbing a גר

steps.title: The convert who turned the theft into a loan, and the disagreement
steps.stepSummary: A man robbed a גר and swore falsely. Later he met the גר, who turned the debt into a loan and then died. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the robber keeps the money. רבי עקיבא says he must still get rid of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man robbed a גר and swore falsely to him. He heard the גר had died, so he was bringing his money and his אשם offering to Jerusalem. On the way he met that same גר, who turned the debt into a loan. Then the גר really died. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the robber keeps what he has. רבי עקיבא says he has no fix until he gives away the stolen money.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells its case and gives the two opinions. This is the מחלוקת that רבי יוחנן said lies behind the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning the theft into a loan is a kind of forgiving of the theft debt. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it works: the debt became a normal loan, and when the heirless גר died nobody owns the claim. רבי עקיבא says the robber can never just keep stolen money and must give it away.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned it into a loan owed by him
That person (the robber) gets to keep it
He has no way to fix it

phrases.english: Here is one who robbed a convert
and swore to him
and heard that the convert died
and he was bringing his money and his guilt-offering up to Jerusalem
and he met that same convert
and he set it on him as a loan
phrases.notes: The גר, who was alive after all, turned the theft debt into a regular loan.

phrases.english: and then he died
that one keeps what is in his hand
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
Rabbi Akiva says:
He has no remedy
until he takes his stolen item out of his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the פסוק to the actual case and the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי הגלילי: once the theft became a loan and the heirless גר died, the robber keeps it. רבי עקיבא: the robber must still give away the stolen money.

steps.title: How each opinion handles forgiving a theft debt
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, a theft debt can be forgiven, whether to oneself or to others. For רבי עקיבא, it can never be forgiven, whether to others or to oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, it makes no difference whether the forgiving is to himself or to someone else: he can forgive. For רבי עקיבא, it makes no difference whether it is to someone else or to himself: he cannot forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out how the ברייתא solves the contradiction from step 4. Each תנא has one consistent rule about forgiving a theft debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that lets an owner forgive the robber (step 5) follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. Our משנה, where the son who inherited cannot just forgive himself, follows רבי עקיבא. That way the two משניות no longer clash.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds a theft debt can always be forgiven, and רבי עקיבא holds it can never just be forgiven, so the stolen money must leave the robber's hands. On this reading, our משנה about the son follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'To himself' does not mean a person forgiving someone else. It means the one forgiving is also the one who owes, like the son who inherited his father's claim against himself.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
there is no difference whether it is to himself
phrases.notes: Forgiving a debt he himself owes, like the son who inherited his father's claim.

phrases.english: and no difference whether it is to others
he can forgive;
and according to Rabbi Akiva
there is no difference whether it is to others
and no difference whether it is to himself
he cannot forgive.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לָא שְׁנָא לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ברייתא's מחלוקת and applies it to the question of forgiving a theft debt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each משנה to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to follow one view, so one allows forgiving and the other forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה allowing forgiveness follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. Our משנה forbidding the son to forgive himself follows רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא mentions turning the theft into a loan
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the loan was not even needed. The ברייתא mentions it only to show how strong רבי עקיבא's view is: even with a loan, the robber must give the money away.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוסי, the same would be true even without turning it into a loan. The ברייתא says 'he set it as a loan' to show the strength of רבי עקיבא: even if it became a loan, the robber has no fix until he takes the stolen money out of his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question it does not state out loud. If רבי יוסי lets the robber keep the money anyway, why does the ברייתא mention the loan?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יוסי allows forgiving even to oneself, the robber could keep the money even without the loan. The loan detail is there for רבי עקיבא: even though the debt looks like a normal loan now, he still says the robber may not keep stolen money.

keyTerms.meaning: And the reason it teaches this
To show you the strength (of his view)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two views are complete opposites. רבי יוסי allows forgiving in every case, and רבי עקיבא forbids keeping stolen money even after it was turned into a loan.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei
the same law applies
even if he had not set it as a loan
and the fact that it teaches
"he set it on him as a loan"
is to show you how far Rabbi Akiva goes
that even if he set them on him as a loan
he has no remedy
until he takes the stolen item out of his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out רבי יוסי's broad view in step 9, the גמרא explains why the ברייתא still needed the loan detail.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why a detail is in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loan detail might seem needed for רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי the loan detail is not needed. It is there to show that רבי עקיבא forbids keeping the money even after a loan.

steps.title: רב ששת objects: the משניות should have taught the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges רבי יוחנן. If each תנא has one rule for both cases, the משניות picked the wrong case to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: If so, then according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the משנה should have taught that one can forgive 'to himself,' and we would know all the more so 'to others'! And according to רבי עקיבא, it should have taught that one cannot forgive 'to others,' and we would know all the more so that one cannot forgive 'to himself'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the answer from Step 9, that each תנא has one rule covering both 'to himself' and 'to others'. He argues that the משניות are worded in a way that teaches less than they could have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For someone who allows forgiving, forgiving 'to himself' is the bigger חידוש, so that is the case the משנה should state. For someone who forbids forgiving, forbidding it 'to others' is the bigger חידוש. Each משנה states the weaker case, so the 'one rule for both' approach looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; a strong challenge from an אמורא
If so; if your explanation is right
Let it teach us; the משנה should have said
All the more so; the smaller case follows on its own
To himself / to others; the two kinds of forgiving being compared

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to this:
If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if each תנא really has one rule for both cases, like Step 9 said.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, let it teach us that one can forgive 'to himself,'
and all the more so 'to others'!

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – לַשְׁמְעִינַן לַאֲחֵרִים דְּלָא מָצֵי מָחֵיל,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Akiva, let it teach us that one cannot forgive 'to others,'

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּלָא מָצֵי מָחֵיל!
phrases.english: and all the more so that one cannot forgive 'to himself'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in Steps 9-10 that each תנא has one blanket rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's answer that one משנה follows רבי יוסי הגלילי and the other follows רבי עקיבא, each with one rule for both cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should state the bigger חידוש, since the smaller case would follow by כל שכן. Under רבי יוחנן's reading, each משנה states the smaller case.

steps.title: רב ששת: both משניות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that both משניות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. In his view, forgiving works 'to others' but not 'to himself'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: Both this משנה and that one follow רבי יוסי הגלילי. When רבי יוסי הגלילי says one can forgive, he means 'to others,' but 'to himself' one cannot forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת drops רבי יוחנן's split between two תנאים. He puts both משניות under רבי יוסי הגלילי by splitting the two cases instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is no longer between two תנאים. It is between two kinds of forgiving. Forgiving 'to others' works, which fits one משנה. Forgiving 'to himself' does not work, which fits the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
This one and that one; both sources

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
This one and that one both follow Rabbi Yosei HaGelili;
phrases.notes: 'This one and that one' means the two משניות that seemed to contradict each other.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי דְּמָצֵי מָחֵיל – לַאֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: when Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says that one can forgive, he means 'to others,'
but 'to himself' one cannot forgive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers his own objection by replacing רבי יוחנן's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same תנא, two different cases ('to others' and 'to himself').
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות follow two different תנאים, each with one blanket rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי יוסי הגלילי: forgiving 'to others' works, forgiving 'to himself' does not.

steps.title: Then why does the robber of the גר keep the money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב ששת explains the ברייתא, where רבי יוסי הגלילי lets the robber keep what he holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why did that robber acquire what is in his hand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רב ששת's new rule against the ברייתא from Step 8. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that forgiving 'to himself' does not work, his ruling in the ברייתא is hard to explain. There, the robber of the גר keeps the money. This challenges רב ששת's answer, and the next step defends it.

phrases.english: But why did that one acquire
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the man from Step 8 who robbed the גר, swore falsely, and kept the money after the גר died.

phrases.english: what is in his hand?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַמַּאי זָכָה הַלָּה בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב ששת's rule against רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the robber can keep the money if רבי יוסי הגלילי does not allow forgiving 'to himself'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that, for רבי יוסי הגלילי, a theft debt cannot be forgiven 'to himself'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי הגלילי lets the robber of the גר keep the money after the heirless גר dies. That looks like forgiving 'to himself', which רב ששת says רבי יוסי הגלילי does not allow.

steps.title: Because the גר turned it into a loan
steps.stepSummary: The robber keeps the money because the גר turned the stolen money into a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the גר set the money upon him as a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in the ברייתא, the גר turned the theft debt into a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the debt became a regular loan, the robber was no longer holding stolen money. A loan owed to a גר who dies with no heirs simply stays with the borrower. So no 'forgiving to himself' was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He set them upon him; turned the money into a debt owed to him

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת, רבי יוסי הגלילי allows forgiving a theft debt 'to others' only. The robber of the גר keeps the money only because the debt became a loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: Here the loan becomes the key to the case. Step 10 had said that for רבי יוסי הגלילי the loan was not even needed.

phrases.english: Because he set them upon him as a loan.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The theft debt was turned into a loan, so it no longer counts as stolen money.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pinning the ruling on a specific detail of the case (the loan)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי lets the robber keep the money because he may forgive the theft debt to himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The robber keeps the money only because the גר turned the theft debt into a loan, so no forgiving 'to himself' was needed.

steps.title: רבא: both משניות follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the reverse answer. Both משניות follow רבי עקיבא, who blocks forgiving only 'to himself' and allows it 'to others'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both this משנה and that one follow רבי עקיבא. When רבי עקיבא says one cannot forgive, he means 'to himself,' but 'to others' one can forgive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to put both משניות under one תנא. He picks רבי עקיבא instead of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא uses the same split as רב ששת: 'to others' versus 'to himself'. But he places it in רבי עקיבא's view. So רבי עקיבא's strict ruling covers only forgiving 'to himself', and forgiving 'to others' still works.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא said; introduces a different answer

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers. רבי יוחנן: two different תנאים. רב ששת: both follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, forgiving works only 'to others'. רבא: both follow רבי עקיבא, forgiving is blocked only 'to himself'.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת and רבא use the same split, 'to others' versus 'to himself'. They only argue about which תנא holds it. Both agree that forgiving 'to others' works and forgiving 'to himself' does not.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one and that one both follow Rabbi Akiva;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּלָא מָצֵי מָחֵיל – לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ,
phrases.english: when Rabbi Akiva says that one cannot forgive, he means 'to himself,'
but 'to others' one can forgive.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the problem רב ששת raised, placing both משניות under רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same תנא, two different cases, this time under רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות follow רבי יוסי הגלילי, as רב ששת said.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי עקיבא: forgiving 'to himself' does not work, forgiving 'to others' does.
